title: Embedded TNs for Answer Choices

illustrates.quote: Picture descriptions are not limited to seven or fewer words.

items.text: b. two boys eating ice cream from the carton

print.printFeatures: The three answer choices are photographs (a girl eating candy; two boys eating ice cream from a carton; a girl eating a carrot) with NO print text of their own at all — confirmed directly against the PDF page image (p.268): only the bare labels "a." "b." "c." are printed, no caption text.

braille.notes: Independently re-extracted from source (fixed left margin / line-number field stripped by counting; U+2800→space; trailing spaces removed); confirmed byte-identical to both run A and run B (gold-10-A/gold-10-B) except where differences.md records a correction.

uncertain: Choice items are built with the SAME wording as the given braille’s own transcriber’s-note descriptions, since print itself has no text of any kind for them (per 10.11.1, a TN description is the only content there is to transcribe) — Emboss has no picture-in-exercise-item TN mechanism (F-229), so this text is built as plain untagged item text and is expected to mismatch the given braille’s own TN-wrapped ("@.<...@.>") form.
resolution: Braille matches both A and B exactly. Print: both runs agree the photographs carry no print text at all; confirmed directly against the PDF page image.
